newsitem.title: UK: Statoil/BP suspend Nigeria drilling, withdraw staff.
newsitem.headline: Statoil/BP suspend Nigeria drilling, withdraw staff.

text.p: Norway's Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Tuesday it was withdrawing drilling staff from Nigeria after five offshore wells failed to turn up a commercial discovery.

Statoil, which was planning to drill eight wells on four offshore licences in alliance with British Petroleum Plc (BP), said it was demobilising eight staff because no new wells were planned before 1998.
Four BP employees would also return home.
"While we're demobilising, we're also concerned to maintain motivation among local employees," said Statoil's personnel and administration manager for Nigeria Eva Stromskag.

"Although the wells we've drilled so far have unfortunately failed to yield commercial results, it's now more important than ever to do high quality work which can help create a long-term perspective for Statoil (Nigeria)."

The company's Status Weekly newsletter said five wells were drilled in 500-800 metres of water and the Statoil/BP alliance was beginning the task of assessing large amounts of three-dimensional seismic data as a basis for developing new deepwater exploration models.
"Statoil and BP are also working to secure a deepwater rig for the next drilling programme, which could include wells in more than 1,000 metres of water," the newsletter said.
Statoil/BP have interests in blocks 210, 213, 217 and 218.
